cause: save()/start() deleted control keys (numFiles, timeout) from the writer's own options dict to keep them out of pandas kwargs, consuming them on first use; freq existed only after trigger()
evidence_loop: pytest tests/test_5_files_write_batch.py tests/test_5_files_write_stream.py: assert 2 == 4 (16), KeyError 'timeout' (14) -> green
expected: options are read, never consumed: every save honours numFiles; timeout defaults to 20 s and trigger has a default
solution: pop the control keys from a per-call copy passed to the file handler; freq defaults to 1 s in __init__ (documented)
symptom: save() does del write_options['numFiles'] so a reused writer writes 1 file the second time; start() does del write_options['timeout'] unconditionally (KeyError when unset) and reads self.freq that only trigger() sets (AttributeError)
title: Writer control options are deleted from the shared options dict on use: reuse loses numFiles, stream without timeout raises KeyError, start() without trigger() raises AttributeError

cause: size had two owners: FileWriter kept its own _size=1000 and DataGenerator resolved its size by copied ternaries in get_df and stream_dict; the writer closures (built in __init__) never read the generator size
evidence_loop: pytest tests/test_5_files_write_batch.py tests/test_5_files_write_stream.py tests/test_2_data_generator_fails.py on pre-fix prod: 20 failed (assert 1000 == 5 x16, assert 1000 == 7, AttributeError _size, DID NOT RAISE RandEngineError x2) -> green
expected: 5000 rows (int or callable size): the writer uses the generator size unless .write.size() overrides it
solution: operator ruling 2026-10-03: delete .write.size(); DataGenerator owns size alone via _resolve_size() (int or callable, re-read per file/microbatch, RandEngineError naming .size(n) when unset) used by get_df, stream_dict and both writer closures; writers resolve every microbatch before any overwrite deletion
symptom: DataGenerator(spec).size(5000).write.format('csv').save(path) writes 1000 rows; FileWriter keeps its own _size=1000 and the generator size never flows to it (README writing example)
title: DataGenerator.size() never reaches .write/.writeStream: files always hold 1000 rows

cause: attacker-controllable GitHub context (head_commit.message, head_ref, ref_name) was interpolated with ${{ }} directly into run: scripts, so bash parsed it as code
evidence_loop: render summary step with e06e526 message substituted; bash -n: exit 2 'syntax error near unexpected token (' before, exit 0 after; actionlint: 3 untrusted-input findings before, 0 after
expected: untrusted context passes via env: and is referenced as a quoted variable; summary job green
repro: render test_on_push.yml summary step with e06e526's message substituted, then bash -n -> syntax error
solution: moved every untrusted context into step env: and referenced it as a quoted shell variable; summary prints only the message's first line
symptom: CI run 37157450889 (e06e526): job Test Summary fails 'line 17: syntax error near unexpected token (' because ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }} is substituted into the bash script before parsing; same pattern is GitHub Actions script injection
title: Workflows interpolate attacker-controllable context (commit message, branch names) into run: scripts

expected: Warning-level findings are reported and validation passes; only errors raise.
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from rand_engine.validators.common_validator import CommonValidator as V; V.validate_spark_and_raise({"device_os":{"method":"distincts_map","cols":["device","os"],"kwargs":{"distincts":{"smartphone":["android","ios"]}}}})' -> SpecValidationError: ⚠️ Column 'device_os': method 'distincts_map' is a dummy in SparkGenerator (returns NULL)
symptom: The ⚠️ glyph is not a severity: CommonValidator appends warning-level findings to the error list and raises (common_validator.py:453-461). docs/2_SPARK_GENERATOR.md:39,127-145 promise advanced methods are allowed in SparkGenerator with a warning (returning NULL); validate_spark_and_raise raises SpecValidationError instead.
title: Validator '⚠️' findings are errors: documented warning-only paths raise

expected: A spec the validator accepts runs on the engine, and a spec the engine runs (including the validator's own examples) validates; one source of truth for method params.
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from rand_engine import DataGenerator as G; G({"a":{"method":"integers","kwargs":{"min":1,"max":5,"dtype":"int"}}}).size(2).get_df()' -> ColumnGenerationError: gen_ints() got an unexpected keyword argument 'dtype'
symptom: The validator keeps its own method/param tables independent of the cores: it accepts integers.dtype (NPCore raises ColumnGenerationError: unexpected keyword 'dtype'), accepts distincts_external (no engine maps it: KeyError 'distincts_external'), rejects its own uuid4 example without kwargs (pandas and Spark), and NPCore.gen_uuid4 takes a length it ignores.
title: Validator parameter tables drift from the engine method signatures

expected: A seed reproduces identical output on every machine (bounds interpreted in UTC or an explicit tz).
repro: for z in UTC America/Sao_Paulo; do TZ=$z PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from rand_engine import DataGenerator as G; print(G({"t":{"method":"unix_timestamps","kwargs":{"start":"2024-01-01","end":"2024-01-02","date_format":"%Y-%m-%d"}}},seed=7).size(1).get_df().t[0])'; done -> 1704128815 / 1704139615
symptom: _np_core converts date bounds with naive datetime.timestamp()/fromtimestamp() (lines 69, 91), so unix_timestamps/dates depend on the process TZ: seed=7 gives 1704128815 under UTC and 1704139615 under America/Sao_Paulo.
title: Same seed yields different timestamps per machine timezone

expected: Values stay within [min,max], or the spec is rejected when the bounds do not fit int_type.
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from rand_engine import DataGenerator as G; print(G({"p":{"method":"integers","kwargs":{"min":0,"max":1000,"int_type":"int8"}}},seed=1).size(5).get_df().p.tolist())' -> [37, -21, -116, 72, -1]
symptom: NPCore.gen_ints draws int64 then .astype(int_type) unchecked; min=0 max=1000 int_type=int8 yields negatives outside [min,max].
title: integers with a too-small int_type silently wraps to wrong values

expected: Every value lies within [min, max] as given.
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from rand_engine import DataGenerator as G; print(G({"p":{"method":"floats","kwargs":{"min":9.99,"max":10.5}}},seed=1).size(10000).get_df().p.agg(["min","max"]).tolist())' -> [9.0, 9.99]
symptom: NPCore.gen_floats draws the integer part with randint(min, max), dropping the fractional bounds: min=9.99 max=10.5 yields values from 9.00 to 9.99, never in [9.99,10.5].
title: floats truncates min/max to integers

expected: Both engines treat integers max identically (inclusive, as the pandas engine does).
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F; from rand_engine.main.spark_generator import SparkGenerator; s=SparkSession.builder.master("local[1]").getOrCreate(); print(sorted(r[0] for r in SparkGenerator(s,F,{"a":{"method":"integers","kwargs":{"min":0,"max":1}}}).size(20000).get_df().select("a").distinct().collect()))' -> [0]
symptom: SparkCore.gen_ints casts rand()*(max-min)+min, so max is exclusive; NPCore uses randint(min, max+1), inclusive. min=0 max=1 on Spark yields only 0.
title: Spark integers never reaches max while pandas includes it
